column1: # Author: Lane #1644 (Codex). Individually read direct uses; canonical selected/owner syntax pins.

column8: Fixture Check demands the exact seeded Engine declare its boundary policy before running independent mode and row oracles; this assertion grants no production read authority.
The public-obligation checker reads the fixture declaration to cross each policy field with executable consumers; it never substitutes that declaration for the issued Engine.
StoredModes checks the fixture declaration independently, then executes ReadStored on f.Engine for each mode and checks actual seeded IDs and structural payload absence.

The fixture cleanup auditor probes NodeCount only when a concrete resource supplies a known closed sentinel. It checks that same resource after cleanup and disposes leaks; it neither supplies a production count result nor discovers a data-read provider. This scalar signature is a real typed match and remains registered rather than hidden by a name filter.

Before changing an administration database, this controller reads metadata from its own active native transaction and rolls that transaction back; it does not recover a data reader by casting a decorator.
After handleBegin issues the replacement system transaction, the controller restores metadata to that exact new transaction and builds the system-scoped adapter.
AStar first calls graphReadArguments, which creates the graph-identity executor over getStorage(ctx); this cast converts the resulting path for output, retaining that issued identity view.
AllSimplePaths uses graphReadArguments before the search; the asserted identity view converts each output path and is not an unwrapped data provider.
Dijkstra resolves arguments on the identity executor before searching; the cast only maps the resulting path back through the same view.
Neighbor-by-hop starts with getStorage(ctx) and deliberately retains an already-issued graphIdentityStorage for edge IDs; it does not select its embedded bare Engine.
For a node-valued APOC argument this cast applies the active graph identity conversion; the input value is not reread from physical storage.
For a string APOC argument the graphIdentityView owns GetNode and input-key resolution; this cast decides only whether its result is already in the working identity representation.
tx.setMetaData uses the controller-owned native transaction when active and otherwise nativeMemberFor(getStorage(ctx)); metadata is written to that exact member, never a read-unwrapped engine.
The read branch retrieves an already-open Fabric participant and returns its transactionStorageFor view; unopened read participants retain the admitted engine.
The write branch authorizes, calls Fabric GetOrOpen, obtains the canonical participant, then returns its transactionStorageFor view; the cast does not issue a second transaction.

Statement promotion goes through authorization and Fabric GetOrOpen before selecting the participant native transaction. The caller adopts that participant adapter and transaction context; it does not independently publish or commit.
Implicit execution first honors carried membership. Its context cast consumes an already-issued statement adapter before cloning; writes otherwise go through the implicit-transaction owner.
The deferred explicit-transaction memory accounting asks the actual running native transaction for staged bytes; it neither selects a read view nor grants controller authority.
After a successful BEGIN, client metadata is applied to the controller-created native transaction; errors roll it back through the controller.

Fabric local storage resolution validates the manager-returned Engine type before the fragment admission path; it returns the selected issued engine or scopedExecutorForUse, without inspecting embedded children.
The concrete composite check selects the router branch, then WithMembership and WithConstituentAccess carry Fabric ownership into cloneForStorage. Non-root fragments use the opened participant view.
Composite USE validates the database manager result as Engine and passes that result to cloneForStorage; no narrower provider or physical child replaces it.
Database USE validates the manager-issued Engine before cloneForStorage; authorization/normalization remains with the existing credentials path.
graphReadArguments obtains graphIdentityExecutor(ctx), then maps node/string arguments through exactly that returned view; its cast exposes conversion methods only.
graphIdentityView reuses an existing identity view or wraps the original Engine once. Returning the existing value preserves its transforms instead of wrapping its bare child.
The concrete composite branch carries the active Fabric lifecycle into WithMembership before graph-function selection; it preserves the router.

The issuance type switch runs only for an unowned original view with an active controller: native uses transactionStorageFor, Fabric uses the membership-carrying composite. Already-issued transformed views pass through unchanged.
Graph-function storage validates the manager result once inside scope.once; matching/default database returns its supplied issued fallback, not a discovered adapter.

Knowledge policy first selects a constituent through view metadata, then uses nativeMemberFor. The direct native cast is limited to the active top-level controller fallback and selects that transaction's schema.
Composite selected-path search first creates graphIdentityExecutor(ctx); its cast maps start/target/end values and final path representations through that same view.
systemStorage validates the manager-issued system Engine and otherwise returns the original executor store; this is explicit system-database selection before authorization consumers.
The fallback lease cast reads only the ReadLease reference carried by storageMembership; live ended/unbound checks precede borrowing. It does not replace the issued data view.
The fallback mode cast reads only the carried StatementMode reference; the bound fast path borrows the same owner without repeating discovery.
nativeMemberFor reuses the issuance/query binding and only its unbound fallback casts MembershipForEngine(engine).Adapter; the adapter is returned for native control, not substituted for data reads.
pendingMember consumes the cached pending-action owner, or the explicit PendingActions reference from storageMembership; publication stays on that actual member.
schemaMember consumes the cached schema publication owner or the explicit SchemaPublication reference; it does not infer publication permission from an embedded Engine.
queryRead caches actual operation adapters per issued Engine. It casts only the neutral membership Adapter reference to retain native state; bound reads remain tied to the original engine argument.

StorageMembership is the transaction adapter's declaration owner. The TransactionContext cast distinguishes explicit/coordinator ownership from implicit ownership while actual tx.IsActive determines live status.

Execution enforcement first asks wrapper metadata on the original Engine, then the explicitly carried Enforcement owner; its Engine cast only enables that same metadata policy on the carried reference.
Issuance stores the original engine separately and casts only the carried Adapter reference for native state.
Issuance binds the explicit PendingActions reference for later action publication.
Issuance binds the explicit SchemaPublication reference for later schema publication.
Issuance binds the explicit ReadLease reference once; borrowing reads its live owner state.
Issuance binds the explicit StatementMode reference once; the issued data Engine remains separate.
transactionMemberForEngine casts the Adapter returned by the neutral membership cursor; no physical unwrap or independent wrapper walk remains.
Transaction clock reads StartTime from the active controller transaction or nativeMemberFor(e.storage). It returns a timestamp, not a data provider or lifecycle permission.

The controller transaction type branch selects native execution only after excluding Fabric. transactionStorageFor issues its adapter and cloneWithStorage executes through that issued view, with lease/mode carried.

A memory-limit failure rolls back the exact native BadgerTransaction already held by the executor and marks storageRolledBack, releasing its running memory once. The concrete assertion is this native rollback protocol, not provider recovery. Merge-key release separately consumes OwnedCapability on the same tx and existing local/remote participant failure propagation remains unchanged.
After the single commit attempt fails, this native-type check controls only whether the error can be marked rolled back; it does not retry publication.

The controller type switch calls commitStorageTransaction for native or the Fabric terminal for Fabric, after rejecting member controllers; native committer discovery stays in the shared commit policy.
Rollback is controller-only and dispatches to the exact active native or Fabric transaction. It honors prior storage rollback and closes the lifecycle without selecting an underlying read engine.

Pending-write cache admission reads OperationCount from the active controller transaction; unknown implementations conservatively report pending writes. No rows or capabilities are read through a child.
Transactional CALL admission rejects active explicit transactions and uses native OperationCount only to choose the existing error classification; it never opens or commits batches here.
Catalog DROP durability uses the common physical-identity owner to find Sync, then establishes metadata durability before deletion. This is a physical maintenance boundary, not a scoped data read.

The adjacency owner explicitly prefixes inputs before consuming a NamespacedEngine child, then applies toUserEdgesInNamespace to both directions; this is the namespace implementation itself, not caller-side capability discovery.

The adjacency owner selects its native shared captureAdjacencyReader fast path only for exact BadgerEngine. Other views keep their own ordinary/historical operation and any namespace projection is applied before return.

EntityCommitSubmitterFor walks only through VisitPhysicalEngineOwners, stopping at the first submitter or WAL boundary. Its native-type switch decides RequiresSubmission after selecting the submitter, not commit capability membership.

Relationship export deliberately requests complete stored entities through CollectStoredEdges when available; its Engine assertion validates the export surface, and unsupported storage retains the pre-existing explicit full export path.
Node export deliberately requests full payload and embeddings through CollectStoredNodes; this is an intentional complete-image consumer, not mandatory metadata implemented by hydration.

Managed-entity preparation uses the common physical accessor to locate the native namespace preparer registry. It does not submit/apply/forward; caller admission remains required and handled stays true on preparation error.
Replay takes a native helper lifetime lease before import/provenance/apply, retaining txnWG through the operation; the native cast grants no query read view.
Recovery restore uses the physical accessor solely to enter the native semantic property-restore owner. No read provider or user visibility decision is selected.

Recovery foreign-property marking obtains a native helper lifetime lease and walPropertySource lock before changing provenance. Physical identity discovery does not bypass a mutation wrapper to stage a user write.
